prompts.task: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation to the Flask service in ./service. Assume no custom business spans are requested.
Instrument the Flask service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving the existing runtime and startup command. Add auto-instrumentation only; do not add custom business spans.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting files when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Initializes the SDK once in a separate file.

Uses Resource service.name and env-driven OTLP endpoint configuration. Preserves a configured non-default local Splunk Observability Studio receiver port for traces, metrics, and logs, treating 4317/4318 only as no-discovery fallbacks and adding no runtime Obstudio endpoint lookup or route-registration dependency.

Configures one current opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging stdlib bridge backed by a shared-resource LoggerProvider, BatchLogRecordProcessor, and OTLP log exporter to the signal-specific local /v1/logs endpoint by default. When only a compatible generic local OTLP/HTTP endpoint is configured, derives exactly one /v1/logs path while preserving its non-default port; uses inject_trace_context=True without a format change on 0.64b0+/1.43.0+ and omits that unsupported argument on older locked versions.

Exports the fixture's request-context warning as one record with its body, WARN/WARNING severity, python-flask-basic resource identity, and non-empty trace and span IDs while preserving the original stdout/stderr or file handlers without duplicate records.

Honors OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none and another explicit operator-owned exporter by installing no local log provider, exporter, or bridge, while leaving the original application logging sink active; only none disables the default Python logging bridge, and another exporter preserves the operator's OTEL_PYTHON_LOG_AUTO_INSTRUMENTATION ownership.

Keeps generic or signal-specific cloud endpoints, headers, credentials, and forwarding out of the application-log path; direct cloud remains trace/metric-only and logs stay local unless explicitly operator-owned. A conflicting generic header or non-local log endpoint disables only the local log bridge and reports the conflict; it must not raise during application startup or disable the existing trace/metric route and original logging sink.
Registers one lifecycle shutdown callback that uninstalls the logging bridge and flushes the log provider before the shared metric and trace providers finish.
Calls FlaskInstrumentor().instrument_app(app) or an equivalent setup before serving requests.
Records exceptions or sets error status where custom error handling exists.
Keeps the Flask app behavior and routes intact.
